Definition: probably from the base of G2949; to bend forward:--stoop (down).
BiblicalUsage: To stoop down appears once, and it is John the Baptist's picture of his own unworthiness in Mark 1:7: "There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose."
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced the stoop is the whole ministry of John in one gesture: the greatest of the prophets bends low before the shoes of the One who comes after him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
